title: AAH-00: Asymmetric Advantage Hunt — recover the selector’s discarded inventory
body:
# AAH-00 — ASYMMETRIC ADVANTAGE HUNT

## Objective

Recover and convert the people, knowledge, alternatives, rights, interfaces, and correction mechanisms systematically underpriced or discarded by status-dependent selectors.

This is the companion program to #416, not another actor-map expansion.

```text
status-biased recognition
→ discarded capability or alternative
→ preserved evidence
→ independent proof
→ low-cost acquisition or partnership
→ integration into a working system
→ useful product or counterpower
→ durable value and field evidence
```

The dominant ecosystem has more capital, access, personnel, and institutional authority. It also carries portfolio commitments, prestige dependencies, category filters, coordination costs, and incentives not to preserve evidence that makes its selector look unreliable. The project’s asymmetric advantage is cheaper updating, cross-domain inspection, failed-path retention, explicit non-links, public and open infrastructure, and the ability to search the inventory discarded by status-dependent recognition.

The reaction is a routing signal. The object behind the reaction is where the value sits.

## Authority ceiling

This issue names a work program. It does **not** create a canonical evidence object, actor edge, prevalence finding, motive finding, collective-hostility finding, suppression finding, commercial claim, publication clearance, or adoption claim.

```text
status-output residual ≠ hidden genius
attention concentration ≠ motive
personnel movement ≠ coordination
similarity ≠ common purpose
silence ≠ hostility
issue text ≠ canonical object
public probe ≠ field evidence
internal proof ≠ external adoption
graph_effect: none
```

AAH rows remain graph-inert until ordinary Clifford review. The program must preserve controls, alternative explanations, counterevidence, and explicit reasons each candidate may be wrong.

## Build-order dependency

AAH follows the stable-ground checkpoint’s append-preserving order:

```text
1. reconcile PR #410 against canonical Sprint 09 while preserving M05-S15
2. complete K0-Q02 and move the frozen denominator from 8/9 to 9/9
3. reconcile ontology and namespace across K0, Clifford, POOF, REAL STEEL,
   Answerable Power, DCA, and estate objects
4. materialize DCA-H01 and the AAH hunt grammar without actor edges
5. resolve publication safety before landing the evidence-lake stack
6. run reproduction, adjudicator, field-partner, and bounded AAH proof campaigns
   in parallel
7. advance adoption only on observed binding correction and durability receipts
```

Discovery and schema design may proceed in parallel. Canonical promotion must respect this order.

# Master hunt record

Every candidate advantage becomes one typed object:

```text
hunt_id
surface
domain
jurisdiction

protected_center
selector_or_gateholder
selection_rule
status_signal

discarded_person_option_or_capability
observed_output
support_received
support_missing
status_output_residual

exclusion_or_discount_mechanism
counterfactual_support_gap
comparable_selected_object

public_contribution
private_rights
interface_or_dependency
custody_holder
exit_condition

acquisition_cost
verification_cost
integration_cost
time_to_value
buyer_or_beneficiary

minimum_proof_object
missing_receipt
alternative_explanation
counterevidence
falsifier

commercial_wedge
counterpower_wedge
field_test_route

review_state
graph_effect: none
```

The **status-output residual** is a hunt signal: how far observed performance exceeds what conventional social metadata would predict. It does not establish hidden genius. It routes work for evaluation independently of the selector that ignored it.

Initial qualitative priority:

```text
hunt priority
=
status-output residual
× consequence
× evidence availability
× option-set loss
× buyer urgency
× transferability

divided by

verification burden
× integration cost
× legal exposure
× false-positive risk
```

Vendor exit, public contribution, rejected alternatives, technical claims, and institutional application packages rank above attempts to prove that an ecosystem personally dislikes an individual. The latter has weak commercial value, high inference risk, and no reason to consume estate capacity absent bounded receipts.

# Portfolio I — recognition and human capability

## AAH-01 — Recognition Residual Registry

Registry of people and small teams whose conventional status is low relative to repeated observable output. Measure whether a person moves real objects from one valid state to another; do not substitute confidence, vocabulary, reach, or self-description for capability.

First proof: five bounded collaborations producing independently reviewable results.

## AAH-02 — Repair-Capable Partner Graph

Record behavior after contradiction:

```text
exposes unfinished work
→ receives accurate criticism
→ distinguishes object from self
→ corrects
→ preserves custody and relationship
→ follows through
→ returns with another object
```

This is an R&D partnership predictor, not a friendship score.

## AAH-03 — Generalist and Translator Benchmark

Test the same operator across three unrelated systems:

```text
acquire unfamiliar system
→ locate decisive gate
→ reconstruct requirements
→ distinguish proof from unsupported claim
→ route tools and people
→ produce valid artifact
→ preserve custody
→ hand off cleanly
```

Measure transfer, error correction, evidence discipline, and time to valid handoff.

## AAH-04 — Personnel and Tacit-Knowledge Routing

Track bounded movement of skills, vocabulary, customer familiarity, doctrine, and institutional access. Ask what tacit knowledge moved, which interfaces became easier, what combination became possible, and which between-institution operators remain underused. Do not convert career movement into coordination.

## AAH-05 — Community-Amplitude Arbitrage

Use demanding real-world adoption, rapid feedback, shared proof, and mutual amplification as non-VC capital. A small external tool receives high-amplitude product context; the estate receives useful infrastructure and influence over its practical development.

# Portfolio II — the lost option set

## AAH-06 — Rejected Bidder and Non-Winner Denominator

Recover complete eligible fields behind awards, downselects, challenge winners, grants, and portfolios. Build a Counterfactual Market Map covering entrants, pre-comparison exclusions, unequal support, decisive criteria, and stranded components or architectures.

## AAH-07 — Failed-Path Archaeology

Recover failed pilots, abandoned implementations, procurement cancellations, adverse tests, postmortems, inspector-general findings, lawsuit exhibits, and operator workarounds. Convert one failed program into a reusable Failure Packet of design constraints.

## AAH-08 — Abandoned OSS, Stranded IP, and Displaced Maintainers

Track archived projects, shuttered startups, discontinued APIs, layoffs, acquisitions, and sponsor disappearance. Recover only where the problem persists, the component remains sound, rights are clear, integration exists, and maintenance is bounded.

## AAH-09 — Boring Seam Registry

Map the underpriced substrate that makes glamorous systems usable:

```text
calibration
documentation
test harnesses
experiment logs
configuration control
maintenance
training
accessibility
evidence retention
data migration
interoperability
incident recovery
parts and consumables
operator handoff
```

The visible system has already created demand for this layer.

## AAH-10 — Allied and Small-State Sovereignty

Build the independent translation lane connecting host-nation mission, local capacity, agreements, disclosure rules, interoperability, training, evidence custody, ownership, and exit. Target capability without indefinite vendor or ontology dependence.

# Portfolio III — public contribution, dependence, and correction

## AAH-11 — Public Contribution and Residual Rights Ledger

Trace what the public supplied—capital, credit support, demand, ranges, data, access, infrastructure, personnel, validation, market creation, and risk absorption—and what it retained—ownership, warrants, data/IP/audit/transition rights, clawbacks, profit participation, public capacity, and affected-party value.

Products: Public Contribution Ledger and ex-ante Residual Rights Covenant.

## AAH-12 — Interface and Ontology Chokepoint Map

Map practical control below the visible product: schema, ontology, identity, API, transformations, permissions, workflow, registries, configuration, audit history, integration knowledge, and accreditation.

Product: Interface Sovereignty Map distinguishing contractual exit, technical export, workflow portability, staff capability, accreditation continuity, and actual independent operation.

## AAH-13 — Exit and Substitution Laboratory

Attempt controlled exit rather than reading an exit clause. Test data export, schema preservation, workflow recreation, permissions, rule/model portability, audit continuity, replacement integrations, retraining, service continuity, residual deletion, and successor governance.

## AAH-14 — Independent Evidence Custody

Preserve source input, transformations, versions, thresholds, alerts, authorized users, rationales, actions, overrides, rejected options, corrections, outcomes, and custody history outside the gateholder. Begin as a signed portable action-packet service.

## AAH-15 — Repairability Radar

Monitor whether notice, direct voice, evidence access, correction, pre-action pause, burden shift, reversal, remedy, substitution, public capacity, co-governance, value recovery, custody, exit, and successor durability remain operational.

Alert on the weakening of the compulsory mechanism, not merely the survival of nominal rights.

# Portfolio IV — commercial conversion and field use

## AAH-16 — Institutional Locomotion Packages

Controlled movement through a known gate:

```text
current state
→ exact destination gate
→ qualifying evidence
→ prohibited overclaim
→ missing-input ledger
→ decision-maker-legible artifact
→ validation
→ clean handoff
```

Includes nomination, grant, procurement, sponsor, technical evidence, application, partner-capacity, and public-record decision packages.

## AAH-17 — Claim-to-Proof Red-Team Audit

Convert vendor, investor, policy, or technical claims into governing rules, required parameters, disclosed evidence, missing measurements, alternative explanations, test programs, and bounded adjudication.

## AAH-18 — Recognition Integrity Audit

Audit whether an evaluator’s comprehension ceiling becomes an applicant’s credibility ceiling. Test evaluator jurisdiction, status cues, category-spanning penalties, AI attribution, support-adjusted performance, attribution symmetry, update conditions, appeal, and independent review.

```text
not understood ≠ false
outside evaluator competence ≠ applicant incompetence
AI-assisted ≠ AI-authored
state-degraded output ≠ capacity ceiling
```

## AAH-19 — Public Probe and Telemetry Engine

Route bounded public propositions through audience concentration, save/repost/send behavior, direct responses, blocks, citations, and personnel events into targeted source acquisition and bounded estate updates. Telemetry routes research; it does not prove motive.

## AAH-20 — Question 4 Counterpower Pilot

Deliberately modest first field pilot:

```text
low-risk decision-support workflow
no adverse real-person action
real operator
real affected-party standing
independent custody
explicit stop authority
published success and failure contract
```

A successful pilot is direct counterevidence against the strongest negative-constitution hypothesis.

## AAH-21 — Cognitive Attention Governor

Preserve active branches, maintain context, run bounded experiments, watch thresholds, detect drift, queue anomalies, request judgment only when required, surface genuine surprises, and return to a resumable state. Measure attention saved without degrading problem choice, threshold definition, evidence inspection, or adjudication.

## AAH-22 — Anti-Capture Constitution

Product requirements:

```text
role-neutral denominator
positive and negative controls
separate fact from interpretation
preserve failed paths
publish update conditions
independent second-party review
appeal and correction route
no conclusion from silence
no status-based promotion
no graph edge from similarity alone
```

The credibility moat is the ability to find the preferred theory wrong.

# Commercial product stack

| Product | Immediate buyer | Core output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Route Pack | individuals, small firms, partner governments | valid movement through an institutional gate |
| Proof Pack | investors, journalists, vendors, public buyers | claim-to-evidence adjudication and test plan |
| Exit Pack | enterprises, agencies, allies, insurers | practical substitution and operating-sovereignty audit |
| Value Pack | public buyers, auditors, legislators | public-contribution and residual-rights ledger |
| Standing Pack | employers, funders, procurement bodies | recognition-integrity and evaluator-jurisdiction audit |
| Repairability Radar | regulators, insurers, civil society, strategy teams | early warning when binding correction mechanisms disappear |

Route and Proof are the fastest revenue wedges. Exit, Value, Standing, and Radar form the durable evidence and interface moat.

# First convergence train

## Phase 1 — freeze the grammar

Create the AAH master schema, disposition vocabulary, falsifier contract, scoring rubric, and ontology crosswalk across DCA, K0, POOF, REAL STEEL, Answerable Power, and estate objects. Create no actor edges.

## Phase 2 — seed thirty candidates

Populate:

```text
5 status-output mismatch candidates
5 repair-capable partners
5 rejected or forgotten alternatives
5 public-contribution gaps
5 interface or exit chokepoints
5 repairability-threshold events
```

Every row requires a comparable control and an explicit reason it may be wrong.

## Phase 3 — produce four proofs

1. One additional institutional locomotion package.
2. One public-source claim-to-proof audit.
3. One bounded exit or vendor-sovereignty assessment.
4. One small external-tool integration using the community-amplitude pattern.

## Phase 4 — automate only common substrate

```text
requirements extraction
source registry
missing-input ledger
render validation
claim ledger
interface inventory
custody receipt
report generation
handoff packaging
```

Human judgment remains at classification, proof ceiling, acceptance, and consequence.

## Phase 5 — field gate

Select one Question 4 candidate where a real operator, affected-party representative, and independent evidence custodian can participate without adverse automated action. Preserve refusal and failure as field evidence.

# Primary asymmetric surface

The defense-VC spine is most vulnerable at the surfaces its incentives treat as secondary:

```text
discarded operators
failed alternatives
public contribution
maintenance and sustainment
interoperability
evidence custody
affected-party standing
exit
public capacity
residual rights
```

It has capital to build the organ. It is structurally less interested in building the independent nervous system capable of telling the organ to stop, explaining what it did, replacing it, or recovering public value from it.

# Operating instruction

```text
Do not compete to become the preferred insider.

Build the alternative recognition system.
Recover the inventory the selector discards.
Own the proof, exit, custody, and correction layers.
Make every paid engagement feed the lake.
Make every public probe route acquisition.
Make every field failure improve the instrument.
```

# Closure rule

AAH-00 remains open until the program has:

- a canonical graph-inert schema and validator;
- a complete ontology/namespace crosswalk;
- explicit controls, counterevidence, alternatives, falsifiers, and disposition vocabulary;
- at least thirty typed candidates meeting the declared denominator;
- four independently reviewable proof objects;
- one bounded Question 4 field attempt with preserved success or failure receipts;
- no unsupported promotion from attention, similarity, status residual, or selection error into motive, coordination, hostility, suppression, or common purpose.

Permitted terminal dispositions:

```text
verified_advantage
bounded_commercial_wedge
bounded_counterpower_wedge
control_case
non_transferable
rights_blocked
integration_burden_exceeds_value
false_positive
selection_unresolved
source_restricted
requires_named_acquisition
```

```text
graph_effect: none
publication_effect: none
adoption_effect: none
```

# DCA Wave 05 · binding correction and substitution positive controls

Parent: #416  
Fan-out coordinator: #419  
Canonical hypothesis: `DCA-H01` at `af26b797ded7e11fc102f0935f71a9282e976090`

## Purpose

Execute the positive-control half of the denominator:

```text
DCA-Q09  binding_update_control
DCA-Q10  substitution_control
```

This wave asks where external contradiction actually became binding and where a system or vendor was replaced without losing data, workflow, service, accountability, or performance.

Question 4 is an experimental member of this control family, but its future receipts do not replace the historical and cross-domain denominator.

## Binding-update record

Require:

- contradictory knower or affected-party standing before consequence;
- evidence and decision-record access;
- independent pre-action pause or stay;
- burden shift to the acting institution;
- correction, reversal, or effective remedy;
- retaliation and route-around record;
- cost, delay, residual injury, and durability;
- evidence that the institution—not merely the project narrative—obeyed.

## Substitution record

Require:

- exact product, platform, vendor, workflow, and public/customer function;
- exit authority and legal instrument;
- data, schema, identity, workflow, and accreditation continuity;
- users and affected parties;
- cost, delay, service quality, accountability, and post-transition performance;
- residual vendor custody or dependency;
- failed or abandoned exit attempts in the denominator.

## Controls

```text
appeal without stay
inspection without binding authority
correction after irreversible harm
nominal exit clause never exercised
vendor switch with lost continuity
successful public or civic substitute
binding affected-party veto
```

## Acceptance

Produce an answer-story denominator that can weaken or falsify DCA-H01. “Transparency,” “human review,” policy existence, or a favorable outcome is insufficient without observed authority and consequence.

## Current state

```text
query templates executed:       0 / 2
binding-update controls:            0
substitution controls:              0
observed co-governance controls:    0
observed value-recovery controls:   0
graph effect:                    none
```

# DCA Wave 06 · partial counterpower and durability controls

Parent: #416  
Fan-out coordinator: #419  
Canonical hypothesis: `DCA-H01` at `af26b797ded7e11fc102f0935f71a9282e976090`

## Purpose

Execute:

```text
DCA-Q11  inspection_without_remedy_control
DCA-Q12  durability_control
```

This wave distinguishes counterpower that exposes error from counterpower that can bind action, deliver remedy, redistribute authority, and survive institutional change.

## Partial-counterpower record

Require:

- exact inspection, audit, disclosure, ombuds, inquiry, appeal, or review authority;
- evidence obtained and evidence withheld;
- timing relative to material consequence;
- whether a stay existed;
- whether the burden shifted;
- available correction or remedy;
- observed institutional compliance or route-around;
- cost, delay, retaliation, residual injury, and later recurrence.

## Durability record

Require:

- original correction, governance, exit, or value-allocation instrument;
- exact leadership, vendor, contract, system, statutory, or organizational succession event;
- successor obligations and custody;
- observed survival, weakening, bypass, expiry, or reversal;
- affected-party and worker standing after succession;
- known costs and transfer limits.

## Controls

```text
strong report with no stay
binding stay with incomplete remedy
late remedy after irreversible harm
correction survives leadership change
successor system routes around prior controls
formal durability clause never tested
```

## Acceptance

Produce separate `partial_counterpower_control` and `durable_binding_correction` denominators. A public report, apology, settlement, or formal clause cannot be represented as durable counterpower without the observed authority and successor record.

## Current state

```text
query templates executed: 0 / 2
partial controls:             0
durability controls:          0
successor failures:           0
works-standard receipts:      0
graph effect:              none
```

title: [SSC-W01] Separated second-party review campaign and zero-state registry
body:
## Purpose

Create the permanent, append-preserving second-party review campaign for all fourteen maintainer-reviewed SSC-H01 Wave 01 observation packets after SG-08.

This lane exists to obtain genuinely separated external review evidence. It does **not** treat the absence of a reviewer as permission to suspend project reasoning, and it does not allow an internal maintainer, packet author, source custodian, affected target, or materially interested institution to self-award second-party status.

## Frozen starting state

```text
Wave 01 packets:                         14
maintainer-reviewed packets:             14
second-party-reviewed packets:            0
adjudicated packets:                       0
reviewer candidates:                       0
review invitations:                        0
accepted assignments:                      0
valid submitted reviews:                   0
review disagreements:                      0
canonical disposition changes:             0
publication clearances:                    0
graph effects:                             0
```

## Separation law

A reviewer is ineligible for a packet when the reviewer:

- authored or materially edited the packet, its maintainer review, or its acquisition supplement;
- controls or reports to the project maintainer for this review;
- is the named target, source custodian, represented institution, or direct beneficiary of the packet outcome;
- has a material financial, employment, litigation, procurement, political, or close personal interest that could reasonably affect the review;
- participated in an earlier adjudication of the same packet;
- cannot disclose enough identity and conflict information for the review receipt to be evaluated.

Eligibility is packet-specific. One conflict does not establish universal ineligibility, and prestige or institutional title does not establish independence.

## Required review receipt

Every submitted review must bind:

```text
reviewer identity and affiliation
packet ID and exact packet/release digest
review date and source-access statement
conflict disclosure and eligibility decision
independent four-gate assessment
recommended disposition and authority ceiling
retained alternatives and counterevidence
missing acquisitions and unresolved questions
agreement or disagreement with maintainer review
confidence and scope limits
signature or equivalent authenticity receipt
```

## State model

```text
candidate_only
invited
nonresponse
refused
conflict_disclosed
ineligible
accepted
submitted_unvalidated
valid_review
withdrawn
superseded
```

No invitation, nonresponse, refusal, acceptance, or unvalidated submission counts as second-party review.

## Review effect

A valid review may:

- affirm the maintainer ceiling;
- recommend narrowing or expansion;
- identify a control or non-link;
- identify a new acquisition obligation;
- record a bounded disagreement.

A valid review may **not by itself**:

- rewrite the canonical disposition;
- adjudicate its own disagreement;
- clear publication;
- create a graph edge, prevalence estimate, racial-order finding, coordination finding, common-purpose finding, or personal-hostility finding;
- advance deployment, adoption, or real-person pilot authority.

Canonical disposition changes require an append-preserving reconciliation transaction. Material unresolved disagreement routes to a separately eligible adjudicator.

## Deliverables

- packet-neutral candidate and invitation registry;
- exact fourteen-packet assignment denominator;
- reviewer-eligibility and conflict schema;
- review-receipt schema and validation law;
- append-preserving failure/nonresponse denominator;
- deterministic builder, validator, adversarial suite, report, release manifest, and dedicated workflow;
- public intake instructions that do not expose held evidence or imply publication clearance;
- zero-state checkpoint report with `graph_effect: none`.

## Completion gate

The campaign infrastructure completes only after its deterministic products, mutation suite, complete repository release gate, publication-safety checks, and clean reconstruction pass on a transport-free PR head.

The empirical review state remains zero until valid external receipts actually arrive. SG-08 remains current unless a canonical authority state changes.

Demographic presence, patriotic language, disparity, or an individual success cannot by itself establish racial hierarchy, neutrality, tokenism, conscious intent, or common purpose.

### Panel B — institutional conversion and counterpower

```text
F08 F12 F13 F15
```

This panel requires official appointment/removal records, dated role transitions, exact decision surfaces, procurement or institutional denominators, affected-party standing, evidence access, stay, correction, substitution, exit, and value-recovery records. Personnel movement, prior employment, shared investors, policy similarity, or a successful selected vendor cannot establish causation or coordination by itself.

- a diverse body with demonstrable independent authority rather than symbolic presence alone;
- a lawful removal or appointment with complete process and effective review;

## Authority ceiling

Wave 02 begins at zero and may retain partial mechanisms, controls, bounded non-links, falsifiers, source restrictions, and acquisition obligations. It may not self-award:

```text
racial-order or prevalence finding
coordination or common purpose
personal hostility
```

body:
## Parent and purpose

Parent: #508 · Program: #468 · Existing public-capital lane: #473

Close the exact evidence gap for `SSC-OBS-0008` without treating interest, Green Light approval, licensing, leverage commitment, portfolio investment, or projected deployment as interchangeable states.

## Frozen acquisition unit

One complete SBIC Critical Technologies cohort from expression of interest through application, selection, license, leverage, investment, performance, failure, repayment, and public recovery.

## Required records

- complete expression-of-interest, formal-applicant, approved, rejected, withdrawn, and withheld-fund denominator;
- exact legal vehicles, managers, beneficial-control and governance records;
- application dates, committee records, scores, criteria, exceptions, and conflict controls;
- Green Light, licensing, leverage commitment, leverage draw, and amendment chronology by fund;
- fund-level private capital, public leverage, fees, covenants, remedies, and repayment priority;
- complete portfolio investment, follow-on, exit, write-off, default, return, and realized public-repayment records;
- named unsuccessful or nonselected controls;
- program-level monitoring, audit, suspension, substitution, and recovery records.

## State distinctions that may not collapse

```text
interest ≠ application
application ≠ approval
Green Light ≠ license
license ≠ leverage commitment
commitment ≠ draw
fund draw ≠ portfolio investment
portfolio investment ≠ realized performance
projected investment ≠ public benefit
repayment machinery ≠ demonstrated public recovery
```

## Matched controls

- ordinary SBIC fund under equivalent rules;
- approved fund that never draws public leverage;
- licensed fund with weak or failed portfolio performance;
- rejected or withdrawn applicant with later private-market success;
- public-capital program with transparent recovery and independently demonstrated repayment.

## Terminal states


title: [SSC-W02 acquisition] Test nested superiority at one exact institutional gate
body:
## Parent and purpose

Parent: #508 · Program: #468 · Lane: `SSC-F02` · Packet: `SSC-OBS-0016`

Move beyond population-level association by testing one source-complete institutional episode in which a deservingness hierarchy may alter admissibility, selection, consequence, and practical correction.

## Selection law

Do not select an institution because it is famous, disliked, expected to be racist, or rhetorically provocative. Select from a declared official-source universe of rules that explicitly distinguish citizenship, immigration status, work status, dependency, criminality, assimilation, gender, religion, loyalty, or an equivalent deservingness category.

## Required chain

```text
explicit or operational category
→ exact selector and admissibility rule
→ selected, rejected, or burdened denominator
→ material gate
→ observed consequence
→ evidence access and challenge
→ stay, correction, reversal, substitution, or exit outcome
```

## Required records

- statute, regulation, policy, form, directive, or decision rule and version history;
- complete affected and comparator denominator;
- selector, criteria, exceptions, overrides, and burden allocation;
- exact gate: employment, benefit, license, admission, procurement, accreditation, immigration, platform, or equivalent;
- decisions, reasons, consequences, and implementation data;
- affected-party evidence and contrary expertise;
- formal and practical appeal, stay, reversal, substitution, and exit records;
- ordinary lawful-policy and equal-treatment controls.

## Matched controls

- materially similar classification with neutral administration and effective review;
- rhetoric without a gate consequence;
- gate action explained by independently documented performance, safety, or statutory eligibility;
- affected party who successfully compels correction;
- category whose expected hierarchy disappears under complete outcome review.

## Forbidden inferences

```text
survey association → every participant’s motive
patriotic or deservingness language → racial hierarchy
category distinction → unlawful discrimination
formal appeal → effective counterpower
unequal outcome → conscious common purpose
```

## Terminal states

```text
bounded_nested_superiority_chain_supported
partial_functional_convergence
ordinary_lawful_policy_explanation
racial_hierarchy_unsupported
bounded_non_link
falsified
source_restricted
source_unavailable
requires_additional_acquisition
```

## Completion gate

title: Research fan-out: Performative synthetic constituencies and exposure-confounded preference
body:
## Research-batch contract

- `batch_id`: `deployment/performative-synthetic-constituencies`
- `parent_program`: #30
- `related_cases`: #39, #40, #44, #46, #49
- `selection_lane`: `ai-policy-public-private-topology`
- `classification`: causal feedback, preference formation, and intervention-provenance case
- `graph_effect`: `none`
- `verification_status`: `machine_proposed_unverified`
- `publication_status`: `blocked_pending_receipts_and_human_review`

## Case object

**Public-interest question:** When a synthetic audience or modelled population influences which message, product, story, policy, price, or option real people encounter, how can later observed behaviour be distinguished from a preference the system discovered, a response the intervention induced, adaptation to a constrained option set, or strategic refusal?

This question survives removal of Electric Twin, News UK, Dentsu, every named vendor, and every political actor. The object is the feedback architecture by which a model predicts a population, the prediction influences an intervention, the intervention changes the population or its observed behaviour, and the resulting data is reused as validation, optimisation, or training evidence.

## Mechanism under test

```text
observed human or administrative data
→ synthetic or modelled audience query
→ institution selects an intervention or exposure policy
→ real people encounter the selected environment
→ behaviour, retention, purchase, rating, complaint, exit, or nonresponse is observed
→ outcome is interpreted as preference or performance
→ result informs later modelling, ranking, targeting, or deployment
```

The causal concern is not that every recommendation manipulates a person. It is that the institution may later treat behaviour generated under its own selection policy as independent evidence of what the population wanted.

## Primary conceptual anchors

- Perdomo, Zrnic, Mendler-Dünner, and Hardt, **Performative Prediction** (ICML 2020): predictions used for decisions can influence the outcomes they predict.  
  https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/perdomo20a.html
- Brown, Hod, and Kalemaj, **Performative Prediction in a Stateful World** (AISTATS 2022): population response depends on both the deployed model and the current population state, including unequal group capacity to respond.  
  https://proceedings.mlr.press/v151/brown22a.html
- Miller, Perdomo, and Zrnic, **Outside the Echo Chamber: Optimizing the Performative Risk** (ICML 2021): performative stability does not establish that the induced equilibrium is normatively or operationally optimal.  
  https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/miller21a.html
- Tsoy et al., **On the Impact of Performative Risk Minimization for Binary Random Variables** (ICML 2025): prediction accuracy under performative shift can coexist with amplified effects on the underlying distribution.  
  https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/tsoy25a.html

These papers define technical mechanisms and limits. They do not establish that any named synthetic-audience deployment caused preference change.

## Known-positive anchors for intake

1. #40 preserves a bounded Times ExplorAItion workflow in which synthetic conversations informed framing, naming, visual branding, communications, and prioritisation while other inputs remained. The existing receipt classifies screening/acceleration, supplementation, and one vendor-claimed bounded partial substitution. It does not establish a performative effect.
2. #39 preserves Dentsu/Evidenza and Dentsu Generative Audiences deployments connecting synthetic audience insight to media planning and activation. Vendor continuity and causal effects remain unresolved.
3. #44 preserves static distribution-matching claims and their public-reproduction boundary. Those metrics test agreement under frozen questions; they do not test whether deployment changes later preferences, behaviour, option diversity, or subgroup visibility.

## Neutral selection unit

One documented workflow containing all or part of the following chain:

1. a population model, synthetic audience, persona panel, recommender, simulator, or predicted response;
2. a named institutional decision or exposure choice influenced by that output;
3. a real affected population or user cohort;
4. an observed post-deployment outcome;
5. any reuse of that outcome for validation, retraining, ranking, targeting, planning, or public justification.

A capability page without a deployed intervention is `hypothetical`. A deployment without an observed outcome is `intervention_only`. An outcome without a receipted model-to-intervention link is `ordinary_observation`. None may be promoted to a feedback-loop finding by narrative interpolation.

## Selection universe and controls

Begin with every deployment recovered under the frozen synthetic-population vendor cohort and every matched media, product, government, research, or market workflow that exposes sufficient intervention provenance. Apply the same criteria regardless of vendor, customer, ideology, sector, or expected news value.

Required controls include:

- synthetic exploration whose output was never deployed;
- human-research-led intervention with no synthetic population;
- a real A/B or randomised exposure test with a preserved untreated or alternate-treatment group;
- a deployment where the synthetic result was rejected;
- a case where observed behaviour contradicted the synthetic prediction;
- a stable workflow with no later retraining or validation reuse.

## State and provenance vocabulary

Every case must keep these evidence classes separate:

- `preexisting_observed_preference`
- `directly_elicited_human_response`
- `synthetic_predicted_response`
- `institution_selected_intervention`
- `intervention_induced_observation`
- `adaptation_or_compliance`
- `strategic_refusal_or_exit`
- `complaint_or_contestation`
- `post_intervention_model_update`

The same event may support more than one candidate interpretation, but the interpretations cannot be collapsed without a causal design.

## Task packet

1. **Seal the pre-intervention state.** Preserve model and version, population definition, data window, prompt or instrument, complete question and option set, synthetic output, uncertainty, proposed alternatives, approval actor, and decision timestamp.
2. **Reconstruct the selection policy.** Identify which intervention was chosen, which alternatives were rejected or never exposed, who chose, what objective or metric governed selection, and whether abstention was available.
3. **Map real exposure.** Record population, geography, channel, timing, assignment mechanism, frequency, duration, targeting criteria, and whether participants knew that synthetic input influenced the environment.
4. **Preserve counterfactuals.** Identify untreated, alternate-treatment, pre-period, matched, interrupted-time-series, or other credible controls. If none exists, record `causal_attribution_unavailable` rather than inferring induction.
5. **Classify outcomes.** Separate clicks, completion, purchase, retention, survey answer, complaint, opt-out, churn, silence, noncompliance, and organised opposition. Do not treat absence of a click or complaint as indifference without an observation model.
6. **Trace feedback reuse.** Determine whether outcomes changed persona construction, model weights, ranking, targeting, option generation, customer claims, benchmarks, or subsequent institutional decisions.
7. **Measure distributional effects.** Where evidence permits, test option diversity, collective concentration, subgroup visibility, minority preference loss, temporal drift, and whether apparently improved aggregate fit coincides with narrowing of available choices.
8. **Audit authority.** Record who may inspect, pause, override, appeal, demand a new objective, preserve an unmodelled option, or require retirement of the system.
9. **Test succession.** Preserve whether later model, vendor, dataset, prompt, or organisational changes inherit the original validation claim or rerun the full causal and distributional battery.
10. **Build a reproducible event ledger.** A stranger must be able to reconstruct the chain from frozen receipts without accepting the vendor's or customer's causal language.

## Allowed predicates

`synthetic_output_informed`, `intervention_selected`, `alternative_rejected`, `population_exposed`, `assignment_randomised`, `counterfactual_holdout_preserved`, `outcome_observed`, `outcome_reused_for_validation`, `model_updated_after_outcome`, `option_set_narrowed`, `dissent_recorded`, `participant_override_available`, `causal_effect_estimated`, `causal_attribution_unavailable`.

## Forbidden inferences

- exposure proves manipulation;
- correlation between synthetic output and outcome proves the model caused the outcome;
- successful campaign or product performance proves latent preference was discovered;
- behaviour under a constrained option set equals consent to the objective;
- retraining on post-deployment data proves intentional preference shaping;
- no counterfactual proves misconduct;
- audience adaptation, silence, churn, or nonresponse has one universal meaning;
- aggregate agreement preserves minority preference or option diversity;
- performative prediction theory proves a named deployment is performative without a receipted model-to-intervention-to-outcome path.

## Acceptance artifact

A conforming case packet contains:

```text
frozen source population and data window
+ frozen model, prompt/instrument, question and option set
+ synthetic output and uncertainty
+ complete proposed alternative set
+ attributed institutional disposition
+ deployed intervention and exposure policy
+ real population and assignment mechanism
+ counterfactual or explicit absence state
+ post-deployment outcomes by evidence class
+ feedback/retraining use
+ subgroup and diversity analysis where supported
+ contestation, suspension, and remedy rights
+ hashes, receipts, temporal windows, and interpretation contract
```

Acceptance can return `performative_effect_supported`, `performative_path_supported_effect_unresolved`, `ordinary_intervention`, `negative_control`, `inconclusive`, or `inadmissible`. It must be possible for the full programme to return no supported performative effects.

## Publication boundary

A static held-out survey match is evidence about predictive agreement under the tested instrument. It is not evidence that deployment leaves the target population unchanged, that post-deployment behaviour is exogenous, that the chosen option set was legitimate, or that the represented public authorised the intervention.

The publication-grade claim, if receipts eventually support it, is narrower: a model-informed intervention altered the data-generating environment, and later evidence was interpreted or reused without preserving the distinction between discovered and induced response.

Until human review and all repository gates pass, every observation remains `graph_effect: none` and cannot create a hop, score, chain, actor profile, allegation, or publication sentence.

title: Independent artifact review request — CS-EXT-BLIND-W25-0019
body:
## Review request

This issue requests a genuinely independent, artifact-bounded review of one Counter-Selector packet. The source identity label is intentionally omitted, although the distinctive historical artifacts may make the identity inferable.

**Independence requirement:** do not participate if you created, validated, or previously adjudicated Counter-Selector Waves 15–25. Do not contact the source subject. Review the artifacts, attribution ceilings, matched controls, countermodels, and falsifiers rather than reputation.

## Current asserted bounded dimensions

```text
cross_domain_transfer
exception_handling
custody
model_elasticity
governed_capacity
non_zero_sum_orientation
epistemic_restraint
```

## Unresolved dimension after matched-control attack

```text
support_adjusted_surplus:
  insufficient_evidence_after_matched_control_attack
```

## Canonical evidence packet

```text
reports/core-thesis/counter-selector-wave-25/data.json
data/project/counter-selector-wave-25-support-adjusted-surplus.json
data/project/counter-selector-wave-25-comparator-registry.json
data/project/counter-selector-wave-25-release-manifest.json
```

## Matched controls already tested

```text
same-event role-adjacent Watergate control
→ co-refusal observed
→ divergent action observed
→ no normalized output metric

Nicaragua joint-mission contribution control
→ multiple principals and large institutional machinery remain causal
→ no person-specific counterfactual outcome

Law of the Sea successor-role control
→ continuity observed
→ mandate, instructions, policy objectives, and conference phase changed
→ comparator inadmissible

welfare-policy revision peer control
→ attributable model update retained
→ matched peer, original decision object, and normalized outcome absent
```

The internal matched-control audit found zero valid resource-normalized comparators, added no eighth-dimension support, and did not contradict the candidate. It does **not** count as independent review.

## Questions to adjudicate

1. Does the public welfare-policy sequence justify bounded `model_elasticity`, or is it better classified as self-report plus ordinary argumentative concession?
2. Do the attributed election-transition interventions justify bounded `exception_handling` after collective mission contributions are removed?
3. Does successor-capable institutional continuity justify bounded `custody` while remaining below direct person-to-person handoff?
4. Does the same rule-bound independent-authority operation recur across materially distinct domains, rather than reflecting appointment breadth?
5. After the Wave 25 matched controls, is `support_adjusted_surplus` correctly left at `insufficient_evidence`, should it be contradicted, or does a bounded support case survive?
6. Which existing support, if any, should be narrowed, contradicted, or removed?

## Required response format

For each of the eight dimensions, return exactly one state:

```text
bounded_support
contradicted
insufficient_evidence
not_tested
```

For every `bounded_support` or `contradicted` state, include:

```text
artifact basis
scope ceiling
countermodel considered
source or exact record locator
falsifier
```

Then answer separately:

```text
direct handoff established: true | false
support-adjusted surplus established: true | false
model elasticity established: true | false
complete operator finding: true | false
field-test eligibility: true | false
```

## Mandatory boundaries

```text
identity-label removal ≠ identity blindness
appointment ≠ performance
same event ≠ normalized comparator
role-adjacent co-refusal ≠ candidate surplus
joint mission success ≠ person surplus
changed mandate ≠ comparable outcome
missing comparator ≠ surplus
self-reported change ≠ universal model elasticity
public concession ≠ implemented repair
successor continuity ≠ direct handoff
seven supported dimensions ≠ rank
internal audit ≠ external review
review response ≠ contact or field-test authority
```

The request creates no ranking, public identity profile, subject contact, collaboration, field test, promotion, or graph edge. A response may narrow or remove prior support. It is not required to confirm the packet.

title: Acquisition packet: News UK matched synthetic-human workflow protocol
body:
## Acquisition contract

- `acquisition_id`: `PC-AQ-NEWSUK-MATCHED-METHOD-01`
- `parent_program`: #594
- `substitution_case`: #40
- `real_case`: Times ExplorAItion bounded admission, merged via #642
- `negative_control`: Nucleus Panel human-companion admission, merged via #645
- `state`: `prepared_not_sent`
- `contact_authorized`: false
- `route_executed`: false
- `evidence_acquired`: false
- `graph_effect`: `none`
- `counts_toward_thesis_evidence`: false

## Target object

One named News UK decision or research question that was processed through both Times ExplorAItion and Nucleus Panel, or an explicit statement that no such paired workflow exists.

The request is designed to distinguish four states that current public material cannot separate:

```text
parallel products with no workflow intersection
synthetic screening followed by human validation
human and synthetic methods run independently and reconciled
synthetic result used without a matched human step
```

## Required evidence

A qualifying response would preserve as much of the following as News UK can disclose:

1. the named decision, campaign, proposition, product, or editorial question;
2. the complete synthetic and human instruments, including option wording and order;
3. audience definitions, sample construction, eligibility, and timing;
4. method assignment and sequencing;
5. synthetic and human response distributions, uncertainty, and subgroup slices;
6. disagreement, escalation, reconciliation, and override rules;
7. the attributed decision owner and final disposition;
8. whether human findings can amend, suspend, or override a synthetic recommendation;
9. whether human findings update audience definitions, prompts, postprocessing, metrics, or later synthetic models;
10. participant disclosure, correction, withdrawal, complaint, and remedy routes;
11. deployment-specific runtime, metric, policy, and validation lineage;
12. any explicit boundary on what cannot be shared.

## Negative and null responses

The request remains useful if the answer is:

```text
no matched workflow exists
matched use is planned but not yet executed
matched use exists but cannot be disclosed
only aggregate methodology can be disclosed
request routed to another team
no response
```

None of those states may be rewritten as evidence of concealment, misconduct, invalidity, or absence of records.

## Authority boundary

Preparing this packet does not authorize contact. A public email address is a route, not consent to send. No message, follow-up, public escalation, or source-subject contact occurs until separately authorized.

## Closure

Close only when the request packet, acquisition registry, validator, adversarial tests, and explicit unsent boundary are merged, or when the acquisition is superseded by a stronger public or directly supplied protocol. A sent request, response, or acquired document requires a new custody event rather than mutation of the prepared state.

## Object

The current public frontier is HV-03: one executed matched synthetic-human study with enough receipts to distinguish architecture or capability from an actual comparative execution.

This contract defines what a real study must preserve before it can be admitted as a complete matched execution.

## Required study objects

```text
study identity and decision object
synthetic system identity and version
human method and sample identity
matched question instrument and option set
population definitions and eligibility
assignment sequencing timing and geography
synthetic and human response distributions
uncertainty missingness and subgroup slices
```

```text
architecture_or_capability_only
confidential_or_source_restricted
negative_control_no_matched_study
contradicted_or_failed_reconciliation

```

The contract must be able to return no complete study.

## Required controls

Build deterministic fixtures proving that:

1. identical topline percentages under different instruments are not matched evidence;
2. matched questions without matched populations remain non-comparable;
3. matched synthetic and human distributions without uncertainty or subgroup evidence remain incomplete;
4. a discrepancy without a predeclared reconciliation rule cannot be narrated as validation success;
5. agreement without an attributed decision consequence does not establish operational human override;
6. a human result can invalidate or block the synthetic recommendation and must be preserved as negative evidence;
7. study-level validation cannot migrate to a changed runtime metric or policy without a succession receipt;
8. participant research rights remain separate from binding public authority.

Passing the contract establishes only that one study packet is sufficiently complete and comparable under its declared method. It does not prove universal model validity, product superiority, causal effect, participant consent to downstream objectives, or binding public authorization.

## Object

A change in observed response share over time does not identify whether people changed preference, different people entered or exited, the instrument changed, respondents complied strategically, or postprocessing altered the observation.

The control holds the baseline and post-period headline constant while changing the underlying mechanism.

## Frozen headline

```text
baseline observed share: A=60%, B=40%
post-period observed share: A=80%, B=20%
```

## Candidate worlds

```text
stable-panel neutral-learning conversion
stable-panel targeted-exposure conversion
composition replacement with no individual conversion
instrument drift with no individual conversion
strategic compliance with no latent conversion
postprocessing or imputation with no observed conversion
```

## Required custody

Each world must preserve:

```text
baseline cohort and identity continuity
entrants exits and nonresponse
latent transition matrix
reported response matrix
instrument and wording version
exposure assignment and timing
incentive or coercion state
postprocessing and imputation rules
observed headline
mechanism classification
```

## Refusal rules

```text
aggregate shift ≠ individual preference change
panel continuity ≠ instrument invariance
reported choice ≠ latent preference under strategic incentives
entry and exit ≠ conversion
imputation ≠ observed response
instrument drift ≠ population learning
targeted-exposure conversion supports a performative path but does not establish manipulation or intent
```

## Acceptance

The fixture must generate the same 80/20 post headline from all candidate worlds, preserve distinct latent and observation mechanisms, emit hash-linked custody, integrate as PC-10 into the Preference Custody floor, and keep dynamic change separate from authority and legitimacy.

## Closure

Close when the standalone fixture, compiler, validator, adversarial tests, floor integration, documentation, and focused workflow are merged. A real dynamic-preference claim still requires longitudinal identity, invariant or crosswalked instruments, exposure assignment, transition evidence, attrition, and causal design.

title: [SSC-RD04-A02] Complete the neutral fifty-state SNAP source-availability score
body:
Parent lane: #620
Parent wave: #615
Validated parent object: draft PR #660 at `54f0450ef6c238b175e5a217aff5e8253e0d9940`
Gate: `SSC-F02-SNAP-01`

## Purpose

Complete the source-availability selection gate that acquisition 01 deliberately left open. Score the same fifty-state universe under one predeclared official-source protocol, preserve ties and the rejected shortlist, and determine whether California belongs to the highest-coverage set without granting it incumbency weight.

This is a retrieval and custody decision, not a substantive ranking of state policy quality, generosity, legality, discrimination, remedy effectiveness, or national representativeness.

## Frozen state universe

The fifty states, identified by USPS code. The District of Columbia and territories remain outside this lane because the parent issue froze a fifty-state denominator.

## Fixed search protocol

For every state, execute the same four state-domain searches, resolving historical agency-domain changes where needed:

```text
SNAP manual policy version history
SNAP fair hearing continued benefits
SNAP sanction restoration counts
SNAP employment earnings food security evaluation
```

Then check the same federal official-source classes:

```text
FNS State Options Report / dashboard
FNS SNAP E&T State Plans and screening materials
FNS State Activity Reports
FNS Quality Control and Characteristics of SNAP Households
FNS state-specific evaluation catalogues
```

Only federal, state, legislative, regulatory, judicial, or other official public sources may score. Search-result absence is recorded as `not_recovered_after_fixed_search`, never as evidence that a rule, record, remedy, or outcome does not exist.

Cutoff: `2026-08-01`.

## Equal-weight scoring contract

Each of the eight issue-#620 dimensions receives `0`, `1`, or `2` points. No dimension receives extra weight.

```text
0  no official public source recovered by the fixed protocol
1  official public route, rule, plan, or aggregate state-level record recovered
2  official state-specific version history, procedure, count, decision, or measured outcome recovered
```

Dimension-specific level-two requirements:

```text
D1 current policy and version history
   current operative manual/rule plus dated revision, archive, or supersession custody

D2 waiver and exemption rules
   state-specific current implementation rule or manual beyond the federal state profile

D3 screening and verification procedure
   operative state-specific screening or verification procedure beyond the annual plan route

D4 sanction and restoration counts
   period-bound state-level count or bounded observed loss/restoration episode;
   full level requires both sides with denominator or reconciliation

D5 fair-hearing docket and outcomes
   public program-specific decisions or outcome counts, not merely a hearing-request route

D6 notice and interim-benefit practice
   explicit SNAP continuation/aid-pending, repayment, and restoration disposition

D7 employment, earnings, and food-security outcomes
   measured state-specific outcome evaluation, not a program description

D8 lawful demographic breakdowns
   state-specific lawful program or outcome breakdown beyond the federal state profile
```

## Tie and selection law

```text
highest total score → highest-coverage set
all equal highest scores remain tied
no substantive tie-breaker
alphabetical order may sequence work but creates no superiority claim
California remains selected only if it belongs to the highest-coverage set
```

Every non-top state remains in the rejected shortlist with its score, recovered sources, missing dimensions, and exact non-selection reason.

## Required outputs

- one fifty-row source-availability ledger;
- one source catalogue with stable IDs and limitations;
- exact dimension scores and evidence-state vocabulary;
- top set, ties, and complete rejected shortlist;
- explicit comparison with the provisional California chain;
- deterministic builder, validator, adversarial fixtures, exact-byte manifest, noindex report, and read-only workflow;
- child draft PR rooted in the validated Wave 01 ancestry.

## Forbidden promotions

```text
retrieval score → policy quality
public rule → effective implementation
hearing route → effective counterpower
restoration rule → timely restoration
published count → complete denominator
highest source availability → best state
one state or tied set → national prevalence
search absence → record absence
unequal outcome → racial hierarchy, unlawful motive, coordination, or common purpose
```

## Authority ceiling

```text
reviewed disposition changes: 0
residual class closures:       0
complete-compact findings:     0
racial-order findings:         0
prevalence findings:           0
coordination findings:         0
common-purpose findings:       0
graph effects:                 0
publication effects:           0
```

Permitted terminal states remain those defined by #620. Until all fifty rows pass the fixed protocol, the lane stays `requires_additional_acquisition`.

## Object

A correct-looking 80 percent headline, valid file hash, valid signature, or eventual correct decision does not identify whether the evidence path was clean, attacked, detected, quarantined, rolled back, replayed from trusted inputs, or left unresolved.

PC-14 holds participant identities, the published A-family headline, the reference proposal, and the clean evidence packet constant while changing the attack vector, detection timing, trust state, quarantine, rollback, replay, correction, and final implementation consequence.

## Frozen reference state

```text
population: 1,000 retained participants
published family headline: A=80%, B=20%
reference-correct proposal: A1
current evidence packet: EVIDENCE-SET-V2
current policy and metric epoch: EPOCH-2
current trust anchor: TRUST-ROOT-V2
clean decision: A1
```

The public family headline remains 80/20 in every world, including worlds where the exact proposal is wrong, implementation is blocked, or a correction is required.

## Candidate worlds

```text
clean authenticated current evidence
source spoofing detected and quarantined before decision
poisoned source accepted then detected, rolled back, and replayed
retrieval or prompt injection that changes the surfaced evidence context
hash-valid but semantically stale evidence replay
cryptographically valid object signed through a compromised credential
attack detected but no clean recovery source available, requiring abstention
silent undetected attack producing the wrong proposal version
```

## Required custody

Each world must preserve:

```text
attack identity, vector, target, entry point, and first affected artifact
source, content, hash, signature, trust anchor, and freshness state
model, retrieval, prompt, tool, and policy lineage where relevant
detection control, detector version, signal, timestamp, and confidence
pre-decision versus post-decision detection timing
quarantine scope and preserved forensic object
last-known-good checkpoint and rollback action
clean-source availability and replay inputs
replay determinism, result, and validation receipt
trust-anchor revocation, rotation, and succession where relevant
publication correction, notification, and implementation consequence
residual uncertainty, abstention, or unresolved state
hash-linked attack, recovery, and interpretation custody
```

## Refusal rules

```text
valid hash ≠ current or semantically valid evidence
valid signature ≠ uncompromised signer or authorized content
correct final result ≠ clean execution path
attack detection ≠ successful recovery
quarantine ≠ rollback
rollback ≠ deterministic clean replay
replay success ≠ absence of transient exposure or residual harm
eventual correction ≠ no prior consequence
unchanged public headline ≠ unchanged exact proposal or implementation state
missing detector alert ≠ clean provenance
```

## Acceptance

The fixture must preserve one 80/20 public family headline across all worlds; distinguish at least eight attack, containment, and recovery mechanisms; admit one clean execution; preserve one pre-decision containment; preserve multiple post-decision rollback and replay paths; distinguish stale-but-hash-valid evidence from compromised-signature evidence; preserve one detected but unrecoverable abstention; preserve one silent undetected wrong-version outcome; emit hash-linked provenance, attack, detection, quarantine, rollback, replay, correction, and authority custody; and integrate as PC-14 into Preference Custody floor v12.

## Closure

A real provenance-recovery claim still requires artifact bytes and hashes, signature and trust lineage, freshness and semantic-version checks, detector and alert records, quarantine and forensic custody, last-known-good state, replay inputs and determinism, correction and notification, consequence, residual uncertainty, and authority state.

title: [SSC-RD04-A03] Replay and preserve all 200 fifty-state SNAP search receipts
body:
Parent lane: #620
Parent wave: #615
Parent acquisition: #666 / draft PR #672
Validated parent head: `2c8803a644ba23abc739136961121a8c8e3cb75d`
Validated focused run: `30724585217`
Validated standalone release run: `30724585218`
Gate: `SSC-F02-SNAP-01`

## Purpose

Close the search-custody gap exposed by acquisition 02 without altering its source scores in advance. Execute the exact four-query protocol for each of the fifty frozen states, preserve the returned result set and official-source disposition for every query, and then recompute the catalogue frontier from the receipted search record.

This acquisition tests **retrieval reproducibility**. It does not rank policy quality, generosity, legality, discrimination, remedy effectiveness, or national representativeness.

## Frozen query protocol

For each USPS state code and canonical English state name, execute exactly:

```text
Q1  <STATE> SNAP manual policy version history official
Q2  <STATE> SNAP fair hearing continued benefits official
Q3  <STATE> SNAP sanction restoration counts official
Q4  <STATE> SNAP employment earnings food security evaluation official
```

`<STATE>` expands to the full state name without postal code, quotation marks, or added domain terms.

```text
states:                  50
queries per state:        4
required query receipts: 200
```

No query may be silently omitted, rewritten after seeing results, merged with another query, or represented as executed from a source catalogue alone.

## Required receipt per query

```text
query_id
state code and name
exact query text
execution timestamp
search surface and result-page identifier
ordered returned results
result title and URL
publisher/domain classification
official-source eligibility disposition
selected source IDs, if any
rejection reason for every non-retained result
zero-result or tool-failure state
retry count and exact retry reason
```

A query can terminate as:

```text
official_result_recovered
official_route_recovered_page_blocked
no_official_result_in_returned_set
tool_failure_after_bounded_retry
```

`no_official_result_in_returned_set` is not evidence that no official record exists.

## Fixed execution law

- One search surface and one result depth across all 200 queries.
- At most one bounded retry for a tool failure; no result-shopping retry.
- Search order may be alphabetical but creates no priority or superiority.
- Only federal, state, legislative, regulatory, judicial, or other official public sources may affect the score.
- Search-result ordering is custody, not authority.
- Previously recovered catalogue sources remain visible but cannot substitute for a missing query receipt.
- Every mismatch between the A02 catalogue and A03 replay is retained as a typed delta.

## Required deterministic product

- 200 immutable query receipts;
- one 50-row execution matrix proving 4/4 terminal receipts per state;
- complete ordered result catalogue with stable result IDs;
- official/non-official disposition ledger;
- A02-to-A03 source and score delta;
- recomputed tied frontier and rejected shortlist;
- closed schemas, builder, validator, adversarial fixtures, exact-byte manifest, noindex report, and read-only workflow;
- exact child ancestry from `2c8803a644ba23abc739136961121a8c8e3cb75d`.

## Completion gate

The fixed-search selection gate may become complete only if:

```text
terminal query receipts:    200 / 200
states with 4/4 receipts:    50 / 50
silent query omissions:       0
untyped retries:               0
unresolved result IDs:         0
score rows recomputed:        50 / 50
ties and rejected shortlist: complete
```

A terminal tool failure remains a preserved receipt but cannot yield a positive source score from that query.

## Forbidden promotions

```text
search result → source truth
search ordering → source authority
no returned official result → no official record
retrieval score → policy quality
public route → effective implementation
hearing route → effective counterpower
restoration rule → timely restoration
published count → complete denominator
highest source availability → best state
one state or tied set → national prevalence
unequal outcome → racial hierarchy, unlawful motive, coordination, or common purpose
```

## Authority ceiling

```text
residual class closures:       0
reviewed disposition changes:  0
complete-compact findings:     0
racial-order findings:         0
prevalence findings:           0
coordination findings:         0
common-purpose findings:       0
graph effects:                 0
publication effects:           0
```

Until all 200 query receipts are terminal and the recomputation passes, RD-04 remains `requires_additional_acquisition`.

title: [SSC-RD04-A04] Adjudicate replay routes and recompute the fifty-state SNAP source score
body:

## Purpose

Convert A03's retrieval custody into a bounded page-level evidence decision. Adjudicate every unique official-domain route returned by the frozen replay, preserve every A02 source that the replay did not return, and recompute all fifty state rows only from page-level content that satisfies the frozen dimension contract.

This acquisition tests **source-content relevance and score custody**. It does not rank policy quality, generosity, legality, discrimination, remedy effectiveness, or national representativeness.

## Frozen input universe

```text

A02 retained source records:                  53
A02 exact URLs returned by A03:                0
A02 sources not returned by A03:              53
states:                                       50
score dimensions:                              8
```

The zero exact-URL replay match may not remove, weaken, or discredit an A02 source. Search non-return is not record absence. The 59 A03 routes may not change a score merely because their domains are official or because they appeared for a dimension-coded query.

## Required adjudication per A03 route

```text
candidate ID and exact replay URL
first query/result ID and every query in which it appeared
state scope inferred from the URL and page, if any
HTTP status, redirect chain and final URL
retrieval timestamp
page title and canonical URL
content byte count and SHA-256
page-fetch or parse failure state
official-domain basis
SNAP-program relevance
state relevance
dimension relevance
exact supporting passage locator or structured field
limitations and does-not-support boundary
duplicate or alias relationship
terminal disposition
```

Permitted terminal dispositions:

```text
official_relevant_support
official_route_only_generic
official_wrong_state
official_wrong_program
official_page_unavailable_after_bounded_retry
duplicate_or_redirect_alias
not_official_after_page_review
```

A title, snippet, query slot, result order, or official domain alone cannot produce `official_relevant_support`.

## Required treatment of the 53 A02 sources

body:

## Object

A judgment, settlement, compensation award, escrow announcement, insurer payment, public `remedied` status, or complete technical correction does not identify whether affected people can act collectively, collect the award, survive an appeal stay, retain priority in insolvency, receive pass-through funds, bind a successor, or keep a payment that remains subject to clawback.

PC-17 holds the incident, complete technical correction, A1 final state, 100 eligible affected people, a 2,000-unit remedy obligation, and one public `remedied` status constant while changing collective standing, aggregation, stay, escrow, payment path, insolvency priority, take-up, pass-through, successor liability, recoupment risk, and remedy durability.

## Frozen remedy ledger

```text
technical correction:              complete
final reference proposal:          A1
public incident status:            remedied
eligible affected people:          100
nominal compensation obligation:   2,000 units
nonmonetary correction obligation: complete
```

## Candidate worlds

```text
segregated escrow, collective standing, complete payment, and successor guarantee
final judgment stayed pending appeal with no payment
unsecured settlement in insolvency with low-priority fractional recovery
customer receives indemnity but does not pass funds through to affected people
individual-arbitration fragmentation with low claim take-up
successor transaction excludes liabilities after original obligor dissolution
full provisional public-fund payment subject to clawback and recoupment
nonmonetary correction completed while compensation remains uncollected
```

## Required custody

Each world must preserve:

```text
eligible claimant population and identity rule
collective, class, representative, assignment, and individual-claim standing
remedy instrument, amount, currency, beneficiary, and finality state
appeal, stay, bond, injunction, and enforcement status
escrow, trust, segregation, lien, security, and priority state
payer, intermediary, recipient, pass-through, and payment receipt
claim notice, filing burden, take-up, opt-in, opt-out, and exclusion state

merger, acquisition, dissolution, assignment, and successor-liability terms
insurance, public fund, subrogation, clawback, recoupment, and provisional-payment state
nonmonetary correction, monitoring, reopen, and contempt or enforcement route
gross payment, durable payment, unpaid obligation, delay, and residual uncertainty
hash-linked remedy, enforcement, insolvency, succession, payment, and interpretation custody
```

## Refusal rules

```text
judgment or settlement ≠ collected remedy
appeal right ≠ unstayed enforcement
escrow announcement ≠ funded segregated account
payment to an intermediary ≠ payment to affected people
nominal collective eligibility ≠ usable collective standing
individual claim route ≠ complete population remedy
gross provisional payment ≠ durable compensation
insolvency claim ≠ priority or recovery
technical correction ≠ monetary restoration
successor acquisition ≠ successor-liability assumption
public remedied status ≠ completed durable remedy
uncollected award ≠ proof of breach, misconduct, or intent
```

## Acceptance

The fixture must preserve one public `remedied` status, one complete technical correction, one A1 state, one 100-person eligible population, and one 2,000-unit nominal obligation across all candidate worlds; produce at least eight enforcement signatures; admit one complete durable collective remedy; preserve appeal-stay, insolvency-priority, pass-through, claim-fragmentation, successor-liability, clawback, and nonmonetary-only controls; distinguish gross payment from durable compensation; emit hash-linked enforcement, insolvency, payment, succession, and remedy custody; and integrate as PC-17 into Preference Custody floor v15.

## Closure

Close when the standalone fixture, compiler, validator, adversarial tests, floor-v15 integration, documentation, and focused workflow are merged. A real remedy-enforcement claim still requires claimant eligibility, collective standing, instrument finality, stay and bond, escrow and security, payment and pass-through, take-up, insolvency and priority, successor terms, clawback, monitoring, gross and durable payment, residual obligation, enforcement, succession, and authority state.

title: [SSC-RD04-A05] Complete the selected California SNAP consequence, appeal, restoration, and outcome chain

## Purpose

Follow the neutrally selected California chain from operative classification through material benefit consequence, notice, hearing, continued assistance, disposition, reversal, restoration, timing, unresolved cases, and measured residual outcomes.

California is selected because it remains inside the five-state highest-public-source-coverage set after A02 catalogue scoring, A03 exact-query replay, and A04 page-level adjudication. It is not uniquely highest, no substantive tie-breaker was applied, and state selection supplies no national-prevalence authority.

## Frozen causal chain

```text

→ work-fitness, time-limit, exemption, or verification rule
→ evidence and exception decision
→ benefit reduction, suspension, termination, or other consequence
→ notice content and timing
→ hearing request and evidence access
→ continued benefits or aid pending
→ administrative disposition, rehearing, or judicial review
→ reversal, compliance, and benefit restoration
→ restoration timing, unresolved loss, churn, or residual harm
→ employment, earnings, food-security, health, or administrative outcome
```

```text
employment, earnings, food-security, health, and lawful demographic outcomes
```
